preconditions.description: The input integer x is an odd number between 3 and 999,999 inclusive.

postconditions.description: The first line of the output is a single integer q representing the number of operations, where 0 <= q <= 100,000.

postconditions.expression: all(line.split()[1] in ['+', '^'] for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: Each of the following q lines describes an operation with either '+' or '^' as the operator.
Each operation line contains exactly three elements: two integers and an operator.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 5*10**18 and 0 <= int(line.split()[2]) <= 5*10**18 for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: Both operands in each operation are integers within the range [0, 5*10^18].

postconditions.expression: 1 in set(eval(line.replace('^', '&')) for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: The sequence of operations results in the number 1 being on the blackboard.
